state-of-the-corpus.Title: The state of the corpus
state-of-the-corpus.MetaDescription: 10 published measured codebases, read together: what they score, what they ship, and what could not be measured.

children.html: Every codebase here was scored under the Codebase Assurance Index, an open standard. A score is a measurement, never a certificate, and these readings were produced by an implementation of the standard.

Repositories are surveyed on their own cadence: once, or every three months, fortnightly, weekly, daily. props.tip:
The median CAI of the whole measured corpus. Every point is one reading taken on the day it is dated, kept as it was taken and never rewritten: a correction is a new reading on a new day, never an edit to an old one. So this line is read out of what was recorded at the time and is never recomputed from today's corpus.

Only a median is drawn. The chart's axis is the fixed [band scale](https://codeassuranceindex.info/spec/) a CAI is defined on, which fits a median and leaves a share or a count to be stated as its own dated figure instead.

The line is sampled to one point a week, and each point is the newest reading on or before its own date. The corpus is read nightly and its median sits still for weeks, so a mark per reading put a mark wherever the median happened to change. The spacing of the marks then drew the data's volatility rather than the passage of time.

children.html: What a country cut can and cannot be

The only country signal is what an account writes in its own profile line. Nothing is inferred where that line is blank and there is no bucket for the unplaceable: an owner who wrote nothing is counted in the census and absent from every country. So this is a reading of the projects whose owners said where they are, and of nothing wider.
